subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement in core, expose plugin/ClawHub APIs for it, or defer the direction for now?
rationale: The remaining work changes durable skill/session state, public config, user consent for archive/delete behavior, and the Skill Workshop safety boundary; source inspection shows it is not a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design boundary first
options.body: Decide the repair-vs-retirement split, storage model, and approval semantics before any implementation PR is queued.

options.title: Prototype outside core
options.body: Keep core lean by proving the lifecycle behavior through a plugin or ClawHub package, adding core APIs only for missing extension points.

options.title: Defer lifecycle automation
options.body: Leave current Skill Workshop suggestions and manual curation as the supported path until stronger user demand or proof appears.

recommendation.title: Design boundary first
recommendation.body: Decide the repair-vs-retirement split, storage model, and approval semantics before any implementation PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Skill Workshop product-boundary discussion and merged review activity make this the best available decision owner from the history signals.
